summary: Intermittent model artifact checksum failures from range-request body rewrite by corporate egress proxy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent "checksum mismatch" errors when the private deploy serving nodes stream model shard ranges from the S3-compatible artifact store. Errors began after an update to the customer's egress appliance in late Feb 2026. Impact: ~2% of model pulls fail at node initialization causing retries and degraded throughput for short-lived workers; user-visible latency spikes and occasional model load fallback to smaller quantized variant. Environment: Private deployment, control plane in a customer VPC peered to Redwood control plane; egress to artifact host traverses corporate proxy/DLP appliance that rewrites HTTP Range responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private agent using customer VPC config (same revision used by customer). 2) Trigger scale-up so serving nodes perform fresh model shard downloads (large model, multi-range GETs). 3) Observe model pull logs for shard checksum verification failures and engine fallback. 4) Re-run with tcpdump on egress path and compare bytes on the wire vs bytes written to disk. Note: issue is intermittent; reproduce rate ~1-3/100 pulls in customer environment.
logs: serving-node[2026-03-08T14:23:09Z] ERROR model_fetch: shard=0007 length=65536 expected=3f8a7b2c got=3f8a7b00 (checksum mismatch)
control-plane[2026-03-08T14:23:11Z] WARN retrying artifact fetch for model=redwood-gptx-4b-quant attempt=2
curl --range 0-65535 -v https://artifacts.customer.s3/prod/redwood-gptx-4b-quant/0007 -> HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content, Content-Range: bytes 0-65535/20971520
investigation_notes: Customer egress appliance (Acme DLP v5.2) reported to be in-line and performing HTTP response inspection & 'range consolidation' feature enabled.

Packet captures show: bytes on wire include multiple small 206 responses stitched by proxy into a single response; proxy alters Content-Length/Content-Range headers and occasionally injects a small X-DLP-META footer (non-printable 8 bytes) into the body for audit tagging.
Checksums fail only when proxy-audited objects are served and range requests span multiple internal segments; standalone full-object GETs are not failing.

Hypothesis: proxy performs body-level tagging or chunk-level metadata insertion after reassembling range segments, but does not update the checksum/ETag header or adjust Range/Content-Range mapping; client writes body to disk including injected footer bytes which causes checksum mismatch at verification time.
Controlled reproduction: using an interception proxy with body-rewrite enabled we reproduced identical 8-byte corruption and deterministic checksum mismatch against same shard.
Customer confirmed recent appliance upgrade coincides with onset and provided appliance logs indicating 'range-coalesce' and 'attach-audit-token' operations.

Related past tickets: SUP-714990 (proxy auth header injection) and SUP-71492 (http2->http1 translation) — mechanisms are similar but root cause here is body-level footer injection, not header rewrite.
Immediate mitigation tested: disabling 'range coalescing' on the DLP completely eliminated corrupted fetches in a 24h run.

Longer-term options: avoid Range requests by switching to single-range full-object GETs at model pull (cost/latency tradeoff), implement server-side validation that strips known DLP audit tokens when present (not acceptable for security), or coordinate with customer to disable audit footer for artifact buckets.

Action items: 1) Provide secure runbook for customer to disable range-coalesce feature for artifact endpoints. 2) Add detection in serving-runtime to validate and reject artifact body sizes that mismatch Content-Range vs bytes written and emit a clear supportable error. 3) Engineering to consider optional checksum-agnostic shim that strips known audit footers when verifying artifacts (requires formal security review).
comments: Amelia Chen (Support): Opened ticket with customer-provided packet captures and node logs. Requested appliance config snapshot.
BrightHealth operations (customer): Confirmed DLP appliance was upgraded to 5.2.1 on 2026-02-27 and range-coalesce + audit-footer enabled globally; will try disabling on artifact path.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Collected server-side traces and verified checksum mismatch pattern; set up controlled repro using customer's proxy config in staging.
BrightHealth operations: Disabled range-coalesce for artifact host at 2026-03-11T18:05 UTC; initial 6h smoke showed zero corruption. Monitoring continues.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Drafted runbook for customer's network team to apply targeted exception for artifact host. Leaving ticket In Progress until we have 48h of clean runs and customer signs off.
Amelia Chen (Support): Notified product-security of possible security implications of customer-side body modification; awaiting guidance.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer disabled 'range coalesce' / 'attach-audit-token' on their DLP appliance for artifact host; serving nodes no longer see checksum failures in the monitored window. Root cause: in-line egress DLP was inserting an 8-byte audit token into reassembled range responses without updating Content-Length/ETag/Checksum metadata, corrupting shard payloads. Next steps: 1) Customer to keep exception for artifact host and engage DLP vendor for a fix. 2) We will add a pragmatic detection in the serving-runtime to surface a specific 'artifact-body-modified-by-egress-proxy' error with injected payload size info. 3) Close ticket after 48h of no failures and a customer confirmation. Note: security team to evaluate any future server-side stripping approaches before implementation.
follow_up: 48h clean run required; customer operations to confirm by 2026-03-14. Engineering will schedule a low-risk PR for clearer error messaging (ref: PR 742) and track longer-term mitigation options in INT-4210. Security review request created.
